claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is demanding on time due to extensive grinding and farming required for progression.

citations.review_text: GG wp easy game just too grindy but worth the long run but keep in mind if only availfor free time

Now do not get me wrong I love this game. It has a great community and the devs are awesome. However, for returning players it can definitely be a head scratcher when so much has changed and your main character got completely reworked, to the point that every mod I own for them is useless for their reworked kit (obviously this upset me quite a bit, especially with how many new mods have been added to the game also, its quite overwhelming). I would love to get back into Warframe and continue with the quests and the lore but I no longer have an idea as to what to do and where to go. With a busy life I also do not have as much time as a used to when I was much younger, to put hours into farming and grinding so I have become a bit stuck. The new updates I have seen are definitely super interesting and I would really love to play again, but I just cannot. Even with doing the research, reading guides, watching some videos, I am still overwhelmed by how much I need to catch up on. Of course I am disheartened, I still love the game, I just wish it was not so overwhelming for me and I had people to play with so that maybe we could help each other and complete the story together. I think this is a great game for a group of friends that all have the same level of interest and love for the game and can dedicate enough hours into it. This is definitely not a game for people with short attention spans or tend to struggle with games that don't so easily give you direction on what you should be doing. I love Warframe, I am terribly sad that I will probably never play it again after years of a break.      

Before anyone asks I was mainly a PlayStation player I have 6000 Hours and counting on PlayStation and only 11 hours on steam when I decided to switch to PC for good xx

WARFRAME: THE ELEVEN-YEAR ACADEMIC DEGREE IN LOOTING & LOCOMOTION
Genre: Sci-Fi Space Ninja Simulator / Spreadsheets in Space / Digital Hoarding Engine

Verdict: 10/10 Combat Fluidity | 0/10 New Player Onboarding

The Hook
You wake up from a thousand-year nap as a biomechanical space ninja clad in sleek, alien armor. You do a bullet-jump that launches you 50 meters through the air at Mach 2, slide beneath an enemy laser grid, spin 360 degrees, and slice five clone troopers into neatly organized butcher shop cuts using a neon sword.

You look at the screen and whisper to yourself: "This is the greatest free-to-play game ever conceived."

The Reality
You finish the introductory quest. You open your ship's navigation console, look at the Star Chart, open the Modding Bench, check the Foundry, look at the 50 different syndicate factions, examine the 12 distinct open-world standing ranks, and realize the game expects you to earn a master's degree in nuclear physics just to understand how elemental damage works.

You open Google and type: "Warframe beginner guide 2026 update 44 edition condensed." You are met with a 45-minute YouTube video, three subreddits, and an entire community of veteran players chanting: "Just complete the Star Chart, bro, the game gets good after 200 hours!"

The Breakdown
The Movement System: Absolutely unmatched. Going back to any other shooter after mastering bullet-jumping, double-jumping, wall-latching, and void-slinging feels like moving through a tub of cold molasses. Gravity is purely decorative.

The "Free-To-Play" Economy: It’s actually legendary. You can earn the premium currency (Platinum) entirely by selling rare digital rocks and weapon parts to other players in trade chat. You don't buy your power—you farm parts, trade with a guy named xX_LootGod_Xx, and build a multi-million-dollar inventory out of thin air and pure grind.

honestly didn't expect to sink 55 hours into a free game after work but here we are, the movement alone is worth it

citations.review_text:
I really want to like this game, spaceninja game with lots of cool stuff. I like that there is frames for different play styles and also just the way that they look. I like the grind thoe some of it is really stupid and to intense. And whoever decided that fishing is a core grind for a frame, eat rocks. I like the story so far even if Im a bit confused, it is building up to something big which is interesting. So I will keep playing for the story.

However, the amount of time to sink in to actually "enjoy" this game is insane! And as a new player it is confusing as hell. I hate when games pushes tutorial in your face but this also not the way, there is none...? When I have to look at videos outside the game that explains the games different systems, I feel useless because did I miss the info (O.o)

And so far, the bosses sucks ass. They are not intressting in the least and the gameplay loop of grinding them for blueprints and matriels are the defintions of insanity. Like when Im thinking of another space shooter game, the bosses there with the music and game mechanicls are waaay more interesting, fun, cool and beating them feels like I did something more. Beating the ender dragon feels better then the ones I have fought. 

For a looter shooter game, having limited slots for your frames, weapons and other such things is insase, why is that even a thing, I have to spend money to have more frames so I can play them  (-_-)
I know you can get more from playing the story and unlocking junctions and the free battlepass but why make it an item to grind. That feels like it goes against the whole getting loot.

This dosen't impact playing the game but why is color behind a paywall, I cant even recolor my furry companien to a darker or ligher color without whipping out my wallet. I would understand if it was a skin that changed the way it looked like but color, really! (-_-)

The movement and combat are excellent. Explaining what is happening to a new player is... difficult

There is a lot to do, which is both the game's greatest strength and one of its biggest problems. The number of systems can be overwhelming, and progression is not always as clear as it should be.

When it works, it works very well. Getting to that point can be a chore.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that crafting equipment involves waiting through real-time construction time gates in the foundry.

citations.review_text: I cant describe how good this game feels, plays and preform. Had no issues with it and i can say its one of the best games i have played even if its free. foundry takes a long time tho

It's definitely not for everyone. I've returned to this game after 10 years to remember why I stopped playing it in the first place. The first 10 hours is a blast, especially if you're anything like me who enjoys a good movement system and viable melee combat. However, the gun combat feels pretty weak, at least as far in as I am, and the game outscales you pretty quick. Even when trying to pivot off of your basic items (which according to what I've read, you can theoretically play the entire game with just the basics) Warframe reminds you that at the end of the day it is in fact a free-to-play grindfest. If you enjoy the grinding and don't mind the artificially bloated real life wait time for your blueprints to finish constructing, then by all means this game is for you, because from what I can tell, you kind of need to do so. It's still impressive how much you can do without spending a dime, though, I'll give it that much.

Never mind, this game rips.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features bugs and glitches, including character models clipping through floors during missions.

citations.review_text:
I've been playing Warframe off and on for the better part of six years now, I have nearly 2,000 across several different platforms before getting a computer, which one of the first things I did was install Warframe when I final got one.

Warframe is not a perfect game, it definitely has bugs and flaws (a well placed Wrathful Advance from the Warframe Kullervo can easily clip you through the floor.) but regardless of that I find myself drawn to it still, I am still not what one would consider good yet, even after all this time, but I still play anyway. It's just simple fun, I love putting together my builds and running missions, doing some Fashion Framing, Playing the story. This game has truly been a constant companion throughout my life, I have played it when I was going though the toughest time in my life and even after I still play it.

It's not for everyone, I personally know a few people who don't really vibe with the super space ninja game, but I do think everyone should give it try at least once, it is a truly a once in a lifetime game, for better or for worse.

I’ve put around 180 hours into the game across both PC and mobile, and I can confidently say it’s a great game overall. There’s a huge amount of content to get through, which can feel overwhelming at times, so my advice is to take your time and enjoy it at your own pace.

That said, there are a few bugs in the main missions that can be frustrating. Some of the commands and instructions can also be confusing, often taking far too long to figure out what the game actually wants you to do. With the number of comments and complaints about these issues, I would have thought they’d have been addressed by now.

Despite these flaws, I’ve thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and would still recommend giving it a go. Just be prepared for a few frustrating moments along the way! especially farming for your foundry items.

(spend and buy plat wisely i can confirm it can be very tempting)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a player-driven economy where premium currency can be earned through trading prime parts to other players, allowing items like inventory slots to be acquired without spending real money.

citations.review_text:
Warframe is easily one of the best free-to-play games you can play with friends. The main story quests are epic, weird, and genuinely gripping—the lore can feel a little confusing at first if you rush through, but once you look into it and reach the big cinematic quests, the story hooks you completely.

​The core loop of cracking Void Relics to farm parts for new Warframes and Prime weapons feels super rewarding, and the player-driven economy makes it even better. A lot of new players walk in thinking they have to spend real money just to get more Warframe and weapon slots to raise their Mastery Rank, when in reality you can earn Platinum completely free by trading your extra Prime parts to other players. Aside from optional TennoGen/Steam cosmetics, practically everything in the game can be earned just by playing.

It's everything I wished hellgate london was, and more.

Phenomenal pve shooter with a great community and fair prices. You never have to pay a thing because of players trading premium currency for all kinds of drops that are common to get. If you do pay, it goes a long way if you exclusively stick to big sales.

For sanity though, i'd expect most people to pay $15 a month or so just to avoid excessive grind and player trading until they get established. Late game players usually are sitting on tons of currency and resources, but they also have a couple thousand hours played or more.

Greatest f2p game, you get to be a space ninja, there's a ton of story content and quests, there's always new content coming out for it, lots of customization for equipment and playstyles and you can trade other players for premium currency after cracking relics for prime parts so you can buy more slots for weapons and warframes without ever having to spend real money. Runs and looks amazing too.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent balance patches and updates have heavily nerfed popular weapons, builds, and mods, which feels counterproductive and frustrating in a cooperative PvE game.

citations.review_text: The recent changes in balancing very questionable and its worrying for the game's direction. Firstly, nerfing fun builds and interactions in a PVE game is clearly the wrong balancing choice, they aren't at a game breaking level that would ruin other player's experience. Secondly, every game mode is designed with training wheels attached, even the level 1000 icebind mode is easy with a correctly build warframe. Lastly, so many of the old contents in the game are just completely neglected and are just left in a very frustrating state. I just hope the devs would actually take their earplugs out and listen to player feedbacks.

They keep nerfing builds that people like and it's quite pathetic in a pve game. Let players farm, let them make their broken builds. Just because someone can find a nice interaction doesn't mean you have to delete it or nerf it into the ground. People spend crazy time perfecting these builds and DE just slaps them in the face every time.

Might get flamed but the last year of content has just been awful and boring and then they go and nerf Acid Shells in a way that doesnt actually fix the problem (Cyte) and leaves the mod feelings useless. The range didnt need a nerf. Acid shells didnt really need a nerf. Cyte needed a nerf. Now hes just doing the same thing with a different weapon just like everyone said he would.

I dont think this is a bad game and its worth playing if you havent, but I dont have any faith left in this company anymore. Every nerf is just a super kneejerk reaction to some event they put in the game and people finding a way to make the grind more efficient. They never make changes that are smart or good. Nerfs are ALWAYS so bad that it kills whatever got nerfed to the point of uselessness. They will do crap like this and then turn around and be like "LmAo WaRfRaMe DoEsNt HaVe BaLaNcE wYm????hurdurrrr"

Some of these have been touched up but it always takes years. Digital Extremes. Extreme is in the name and they will never fail to have the most Extreme visceral reaction to nerfing stuff into oblivion because they are upset that players will find fun things in their game. 

Gonna take one out of their book and have an Extreme kneejerk and just stop playing the game for good. Thanks for 10 years of fun. Keep up the good work DE! Cant wait to see more news in the future of you nerfing everything but the problem again! Youve never failed to do it!!! :)

Im making this post out of deep affection for Warframe a game I've put years into and used to recommend to everyone. But lately, watching new content launch you can really see the dev's are going in a wrong direction. We get lackluster events, buggy content updates that need immediate day one emergency fixes like the constelations railjack mission, and a steady stream of nerfs that target the very things making gameplay enjoyable eg sobek, jade stars, Steel essance jailjack farming. In a PvE game finding creative, overpowered, or unique builds is the fun. Removing those interactions makes the game feel boring and restrictive. I don't want to see a game I love go downhill, but the current update cycle is making it really hard to hold onto the passion I used to have.
